hlni.insight: Actual program content is defined by specific modules, not the degree title.
hlni.audienceGap: Students often assume B.Com and BBA represent fixed, mutually exclusive career paths.
hlni.viewerChange: The student stops relying on hearsay and starts looking for specific module lists to evaluate their personal fit.
hlni.support: Degree titles are broad categories; curricula vary significantly between institutions. Comparing task-oriented modules provides a more accurate assessment of individual student interest.
hlni.payoff: The student realizes that checking the actual module list is a practical method to make an informed choice.

reelTitle: B.Com vs BBA: The Module Comparison Method
objective: Teach students to compare B.Com and BBA by inspecting specific module lists rather than relying on stereotypes.
targetAudience: A broad +2 student audience discovering ideas, courses, or student experiences

shots.name: The Dorm Room Dilemma
shots.visual: Two students sitting at a table with two physical paper lists labelled 'B.Com' and 'BBA'.
shots.dialogue: Everyone says B.Com is for accounting and BBA is for strategy. But look at these module lists.
shots.cameraPerformance: Close-up on the papers, panning slowly between them.

shots.name: The Module Hunt
shots.visual: A finger pointing to specific line items on the B.Com paper and then the BBA paper, highlighting overlaps.
shots.dialogue: Ignore the labels. Find the actual modules. See how much these core topics overlap? That’s where your real interest lies.
shots.cameraPerformance: Tight macro shot focusing on the text, shifting focus between the two papers.

shots.name: The Informed Decision
shots.visual: The student circles one specific module on each, looking at their friend with a confident realization.
shots.dialogue: Compare the tasks, not the degree name. Choose the syllabus that actually fits what you want to practice daily.

productionNotes.sound: Natural ambient room noise, crisp voiceover

creativeSummary.keyCreativeIdea: Shifting the student's focus from degree labels to the tangible reality of specific module content.
